question: How should a teacher handle a view that will be refuted later in the exposition?
premises: Any point that enters the discussion must be treated seriously.
A position to be refuted later should still be stated with strong reasoning.
inference: Even a future target of refutation should be presented forcefully and clearly when it arises in the explanation.
plain_english: Whatever point comes up in the course of explanation, even if it is to be refuted later, should be presented strongly and supported with very firm reasoning.
